title: Senior sponsor brief and customer quarterly recap email template
content:
Purpose:
This one-pager + email playbook is designed for CSMs preparing a 15–20 minute senior sponsor check-in and a concise customer-facing quarterly recap email. Goal: make it fast to assemble a high-impact update that highlights outcomes, surface risks, and drives renewal/expansion asks with clear next steps.

Audience:
- Primary: Senior sponsors (VP+), procurement stakeholders, and project leads at customer orgs.
- Secondary: Internal account execs, solutions engineers, product manager stakeholders.

TL;DR guidance (for CSMs):
- Lead with business impact: open with 2 bullets that quantify outcomes this quarter.
- Keep the meeting to 15–20 minutes with a 5-minute decision/ask block.
- Use the template email within 24 hours after the meeting.
- Attach a short renewal timeline and single-page checklist.

One-page sponsor brief (talking points) — 6 sections (aim to speak for ~10–12 minutes):
1) Quick intro (45–60s): 
   - "Thanks for your time — we’ll do a quick health snapshot, share wins, and ask for guidance on a small list of decisions."
   - State meeting objective: e.g., "Confirm roadmap prioritization and next steps toward contract renewal in Q2."

2) Business outcomes (2 bullets, 90s):
   - Metric-driven impact: "Reduced inference latency for core customer flow by 27% which led to a 15% lift in completion rate on X widget (Feb–Mar)."
   - Monetizable/operational outcomes: "Per-token spend down 18% vs prior quarter via batching & quantization profile; projected run-rate savings $X/month."

3) Health snapshot (60–90s):
   - Usage trend (weekly active routes, tokens/day): green / yellow / red label.
   - Error rate & SLO adherence: 99.6% availability, 120ms median latency.
   - Top 3 risks: model quality drift on NLU intent A; seasonality causing burst throughput; upcoming infra maintenance window in us-west-2.

4) Recent deliverables and wins (2 minutes):
   - Brief list of shipped items: dedicated capacity scaled to 2x; rollback guardrails added; prompt evals run showing stabilized F1 on intent A.
   - Customer quote or internal metric callout.

5) Ask / decisions (2 minutes):
   - Example asks: approve 6-month reserve for Dedicated GPU pool; greenlight pilot of Redwood Optimize recommendations; sign-off on data-processing addendum.
   - Level-of-effort and impact callouts for each ask.

6) Roadmap & renewal timeline (2 minutes):
   - Next milestones: private deployment PoC, integration of new model variant, enable audit logging.
   - Renewal checkpoint: initial renewal proposal to be shared by 2026-04-15; preferred timeline for signature by 2026-05-15 to avoid rate change.

Meeting agenda (15–20 minutes):
- 0:00–0:02 — Welcome & objective
- 0:02–0:06 — Business outcomes & usage highlights
- 0:06–0:09 — Health snapshot (metrics + risks)
- 0:09–0:12 — Wins & operational improvements
- 0:12–0:15 — Decisions & asks
- 0:15–0:18 — Roadmap & renewal timeline
- 0:18–0:20 — Next steps & close

Sponsor one-pager leave-behind (single page to attach after meeting):
- Top line impact (two bullets)
- 3 health metrics (usage, availability, SLOs)
- 2 asks with short descriptions and timelines
- Renewal timeline (three dates)
- 1 owner and next meeting date

Customer-facing quarterly recap email template (send within 24 hours):
Subject: Q1 Recap & next steps — [Customer] x Redwood Inference
Hi [Sponsor name],

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our check-in: 

What went well this quarter
- Outcome 1 (quantified): e.g., "API latency down 27% on X flow (Feb–Mar), improving customer conversion."
- Outcome 2 (operational): e.g., "Per-token cost reduced 18% via batching and quantization; projected $X/month savings."

Top items to watch
- Risk 1: "Model drift on intent A — we have a mitigation plan to run targeted evals weekly and ship prompt tune by 2026-03-30."
- Risk 2: "Scheduled infra maintenance in us-west-2: low risk but brief elevated latencies possible on 2026-03-22."

Decisions & asks (explicit callouts)
- Approve 6-month Dedicated reserve to secure capacity for seasonal spikes (decision due 2026-04-05).
- Confirm pilot scope for Redwood Optimize recommendations (agree to PoC by 2026-04-01).

Next steps & owners
- CSM (Sophie Lin): share detailed renewal proposal by 2026-03-15 (attachment).
- Solutions Engineer (Diego Morales): schedule deep-dive on model tuning the week of 2026-03-22.
- Customer Action: confirm decision on Dedicated reserve by 2026-04-05.

Quick attach: one-page sponsor brief and renewal checklist (attached).

Thanks,
Sophie Lin
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Renewal checklist (simple actionable items CSM uses to track progress):
- [ ] Confirm renewal owner at customer (name + email)
- [ ] Capture contract constraints (PO timing, legal lead)
- [ ] Share baseline usage & cost report (last 12 weeks)
- [ ] Present three pricing scenarios (renew, expand, committed discount)
- [ ] Run impact deck with executive sponsor (date scheduled)
- [ ] Log renewal in CRM with expected close date and risk bucket
- [ ] If renewal > $100k ARR, flag for AE involvement and legal review

Quarterly metrics snapshot (CSM prep notes — what to pull before meeting):
- WAU/DAU for key API routes (CSV export)
- Median & p95 latency by route, last 30 days
- Token consumption by model & cost breakdown
- Error rates & top error classes (chart)
- Prompt evals summary (F1, BLEU, human-score if available)

Common sponsor questions + succinct answers (prep cheat-sheet):
- "Are we on track for renewal?" — "Yes, current usage and engagement indicate strong value; pending decision on reserves. We’ll deliver a proposal by 2026-03-15."
- "How do you measure quality regressions?" — "We run weekly evals against a curated prompt set and have regression alerts tied to prompt sets in Redwood Optimize."
- "What happens if latency spikes during Black Friday?" — "We maintain surge capacity policies and can failover to a compatible model variant to preserve SLA."

Internal follow-up template after customer email (for CSM to send internally):
Subject: Customer [Customer] — sponsor recap + renewal next steps
Body:
- Recap of asks and deadlines
- Owner assignments (AE, SE, Legal)
- Items needing exec attention (list)
- Link to one-pager & renewal proposal (Confluence/Jira)

Notes and tips from field (CSM playbook learnings):
- Sponsors prefer single-number headlines (e.g., "$X saved / 18% latency reduction") rather than long technical detail.
- Bring one decision per meeting — overloaded ask lists delay sign-off.
- When asking for capacity commitments, surface cost delta and risk of not reserving (queue times, price increases).
- Keep legal/compliance asks as separate follow-ups with a clear owner; sponsors rarely want to read legal text in the meeting.

Attachments to include in final email (checklist)
- One-page sponsor brief (PDF)
- Renewal proposal (pricing scenarios)
- Metrics export (CSV summary)
- Link to prompt eval dashboard (Confluence link)

Template version history and notes:
- v0.1 2026-01-20 Sophie Lin initial draft
- v0.2 2026-02-08 Priya Nair added renewal checklist and internal follow-up template
- v0.3 2026-03-01 Diego Morales updated metrics snapshot guidance and SE asks

Open questions (to resolve before marking final):
- Who at legal owns standard DPA review turnaround times? (action: AE to confirm)
- Confirm preferred file format for sponsor attachments (PDF vs PPT).

End of document.
